title: Powertrain Engineer
jobDescription:
Qualification: B.E/M.E – Mechanical/Automobile
Experience: 4 To 6 Year(s)
Skill set: CATIA V5, 3DX, Teamcenter, GDT & Stack up
Domain knowledge:
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering / Automobile Engineering with 4 to 6 years of relevant professional experience in commodities such as Engine, Transmission, Driveline, Exhaust and other Powertrain related systems
• Demonstrated hands-on experience in CAD modelling, Design proposals, Remastering, vehicle-level packaging, Design rule studies, Assembly maintenance, Tolerance stack-up analysis, Drawing Creation & Checking, Engineering change management & Release Activities
• Strong technical knowledge and proven ability to apply Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) in Engineering drawings per ASME standards
• Maintain and structure component and assembly data within the Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) system and associated engineering-release processes
• Excellent written, verbal communication and technical presentation skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office tools
• Take ownership and collaborate directly (1:1) with cross-functional engineering teams to quickly understand technical requirements, prioritize activities effectively, and deliver high-quality results within program timelines
• Candidates with relevant experience and a shorter notice period will be considered as an added advantage
Job Description:
We are seeking a highly skilled CAD Design Engineer with strong experience in Powertrain/Underbody commodities, including Engine, Transmission, Driveline, Exhaust, and associated systems. candidate will be responsible for independently executing CAD design, Packaging, Design Rules Validation, Integration, Release, and Change-management activities in accordance with Product-development processes & program requirements.

• Execute 3D modelling of components and author complex assemblies using CATIA V5/V6
• Develop and evaluate multiple design proposals and iterations to meet functional, manufacturing, packaging, and program requirements
• Perform CAD remastering from native CAD files without loss of data and parametric integrity
• Create & maintain component and assembly data within the Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) system
• Perform Powertrain packaging and integration studies for affected components/assemblies using surrogate parts at the vehicle level
• Conduct Clearance, Interference, and Design-rule-check analyses to identify and resolve potential design concerns
• Perform Fastener, Linear, and Radial tolerance stack-up analyses at both component and assembly levels
• Create detailed new Component and Assembly drawings for Prototype and Initial Release Builds/Milestones
• Update 3D Models and 2D Engineering drawings in response to approved Engineering Change Notices (ECNs)
• check drawing prints for strict compliance with Ford Drafting Standards and ASME GD&T standards
• Complete the Initial and Post P release activities for Notices covering affected new tool-end items, as well as previously released parts and assemblies

title: Powertrain Integration & NPD CAD
jobDescription:
Qualification: B.E – Mechanical
Experience: 6 To 8 Year(s)
Skill set: Powertrain Integration, NPD CAD, CATIA & 3DEXP
Domain knowledge:
Domain Knowledge & Skills
  • BE/ME in Mechanical or Automobile Engineering with 6 to 8 years of experience (candidates with up to 10 years of experience may also be considered) in powertrain systems (Transmission, Air Intake, Fuel, and Cooling Systems) and vehicle-level propulsion integration.
  • Strong exposure to manufacturing processes: Casting, Machining, Plastic Molding, and Sheet Metal design.
  • Proven experience in vehicle packaging and interface management across chassis, body, and electrical subsystems for propulsion components (engine, transmission, e-drive, battery, inverter, cooling systems).
  • Working knowledge of thermal management and NVH considerations as they relate to cooling, exhaust, and airflow routing — with ability to collaborate cross-functionally with CAE and thermal teams.
  • Proficient in CAD software (typically CATIA V5/3DExperience) and Teamcenter PLM for Ford release processes; strong hands-on modeling capability across Air Intake, Fuel, and Cooling system commodities.
  • Deep understanding of ASME Y14.5 GD&T standards.
  • Experience with DMU (Digital Mock-Up) studies, clearance/interference checks, and static/dynamic simulation tools to validate design rule compliance.
  • Must have hands-on experience in CATIA V5/3DExperience.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across global, cross-functional, and supplier teams.
Job Description:
Role Overview
  • We are looking for a versatile, highly skilled Powertrain Integration & Packaging Engineer to act as a core pillar of our offshore engineering team. This individual will bridge the gap between powertrain design (engines, motors, transmissions, batteries) and the overall vehicle — from early-stage concept design and advanced dimensional engineering to vehicle-level packaging, global stakeholder collaboration, and supplier management. The role ensures propulsion systems fit seamlessly into the chassis, meeting design rule requirements and performance targets by optimizing space, weight, and manufacturability.
Key Responsibilities
Design & Development
  • Lead concept design studies for new product development, design enhancements for efficiency improvement, and provide design support from concept through production validation across Powertrain commodities (Engine, Transmission, Driveline, Air Intake, Cooling, Fuel, Exhaust, and Electrical systems).
  • Handle Powertrain Packaging in the vehicle environment; redesign Exhaust/Fuel systems per new Homologation requirements.
  • Develop packaging concepts for Powertrain commodities.
  • Vehicle Packaging & Integration
  • Develop and maintain 3D packaging of propulsion components (engine, transmission, e-drive, battery, inverter, and cooling systems) to ensure optimal fitment within the vehicle environment.
  • Define and manage technical interface specifications across subsystems (chassis, body, and electrical) to ensure seamless integration of propulsion systems.
  • Optimize space, weight, and manufacturability while balancing performance targets across the vehicle architecture.
Dimensional Engineering
  • Independently perform complex GD&T application, linear/radial/bolt stack-up analysis, and VSA (Variation Systems Analysis).
  • Packaging & DMU
  • Conduct robust DPA (Digital Pre-Assembly) clearance and interference checks of parts against surrounding environments relative to established OEM design rules.
  • Perform Digital Mock-Up (DMU) studies, clearance checks, and static/dynamic simulations to ensure design rule guidelines are met
  • Thermal & NVH Optimization
  • Collaborate with CAE and thermal teams to route cooling hoses, exhaust, and airflow for optimal temperature control and reduced vibration/noise.
Release & Lifecycle Management
  • Drive the Engineering Change Management process, managing end-to-end 2D/3D CAD data releases as per Ford engineering standards using CAD and PLM tools such as CATIA V5 & Teamcenter.
  • Supplier & OEM Collaboration
  • Interact with cross-functional global engineers to resolve technical issues.
  • Guide suppliers to deliver 3D/2D CAD models and drawings compliant

title: NPD - Body Structures [BIW]
jobDescription:
Qualification: BE, BTECH, ME, MTECH
Experience: 5 To 12 Year(s)
Skill set:
5+ years in sheetmetal design for Body Systems. Expert in CATIA V5 and automotive GD&T. Strong knowledge of stamping, forming, and material behavior (HSS, AHSS, aluminum). Skilled in tolerance analysis, assembly fit, and manufacturing collaboration. Proficient with Teamcenter PLM and Vismockup. Experienced in welding and joining methods for structural integrity. Self-motivated with excellent problem-solving and communication skills.
Domain knowledge:
BIW Upper Body Structural Components: The upper body controls vehicle rigidity, crash management, and interior packaging. Experts must master these individual sub-assemblies:
  • A-Pillar: Manages front-offset crashes and roof crush. It must balance high structural strength with a slim profile to minimize the driver's blind spot (obstruction angle).
  • B-Pillar: The primary defense against side impacts. It features a tailored-welded blank design, using ultra-high-strength steel (UHSS) at the top to prevent cabin intrusion and softer steel at the bottom to absorb energy.
  • C/D-Pillars: Tie the roof side rails into the rear wheel houses and quarter panels, controlling torsional rigidity and rear-impact management.
  • Geometric & Packaging Interface Rules Upper body design is heavily constrained by surrounding vehicle systems. Engineers must build and maintain Master Sections according to strict geometric clearances:
  • Vision & Glass Clearance: Maintaining precise margins for the windshield and backlight seating, including space for structural adhesives (polyurethane beads) and flush styling lines.
  • Interior Trim & Airbags: Providing drop-off and clearance zones for the headliner, pillar trims, and the deployment trajectory of Side Curtain Airbags (SAB).Seating & Ergonomics: Adhering to the Ergonomic Hardpoints (H-Point, eye ellipse, and headroom clearances) to ensure the sheet metal does not infringe on passenger space.
  • Closures Matching: Defining the sealing perimeter (flange design) for doors and liftgates to guarantee water-tightness and wind-noise prevention via rubber seals.
  • Manufacturing Feasibility (DFM)A flawless CAD model is useless if it cannot be built. Experts must design with the stamping press and assembly line in mind:Formability: Setting correct draw angles (usually >3 to 5 degrees), minimum fillet radii to prevent splitting, and accounting for material springback during stamping.
  • Flange Design: Engineering mating flanges (typically 12mm to 16mm wide) to give industrial robots enough clearance for spot-welding guns or laser-brazing optics.
  • Weldability & Pitch: Designing proper weld stacks (ideally 2-thickness or 3-thickness sheet metal maximum) and spacing spot welds (typically 30mm to 50mm pitch) to maintain structural integrity without distorting the metal.
  • Corrosion Protection: Adding e-coat hole locations to ensure paint and anti-corrosion fluids can drain completely from closed structural cavities during the dipping process.
  • Crash, Safety, and Material Strategy The upper body dictates the vehicle's safety ratings (e.g., Euro NCAP, IIHS, FMVSS).
  • Load Path Management: Designing continuous, un-interrupted pathways so crash kinetic energy transfers smoothly from the bumper rings, through the pillars, and into the rocker panels.
  • Regulatory Compliance: Specifically engineering for FMVSS 216 / 216a (Roof Crush Resistance) and FMVSS 201 (Upper Interior Head Impact Protection).
  • Advanced Materials: Utilizing a multi-material mix. This includes Boron steel (hot-stamped) for safety cages, Dual-Phase (DP) steels for energy absorption, and Aluminum (6000-series) for lightweight roof panels to lower the vehicle's center of gravity.
Job Description:
  • Design complex BIW upper body structures, including A/B/C/D pillars, roof bows, header rails, and roof panels using advanced surface and solid modeling.
  • Master Section Creation: Develop and maintain master sections to define packaging space, interfaces, and clearance with interior trim, airbags, and glass.
  • Design for Manufacturing (DFM): Conduct formability and tooling feasibility reviews for sheet metal stamping, deep drawing, and joining technologies (spot welding, structural adhesives, laser brazing).
  • Safety & Compliance: Optimize designs to meet global crash and safety requirements, including roof crush (FMVSS 216), side impact, and upper interior head impact.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Interface with the Styling studio to resolve geometric conflicts and work with CAE teams to implement structural reinforcement modifications.
  • GD&T & Tolerancing: Apply Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) principles and perform tolerance stack-up analysis to ensure proper vehicle assembly.
